title: Tavily API Pricing: Credits and Rate Limits (2026)
summary: Tavily API provides web search for AI applications. Get the pricing details, rate limits, error codes, and integration requirements you need.
body_markdown:
## Call Tavily endpoints without code using Activepieces


Without writing any code, you can run Tavily Search or Extract on a schedule in Activepieces, which allows unlimited flows on every plan, including the free one with 1,000 Activepieces credits a month.


It's a workflow tool where you chain steps together on a visual canvas, and it keeps the failure handling from the last section on the canvas instead of buried in a script.


If nobody on your team writes code, this is the cheaper route. Doing nothing means a weekly research job gets done by hand, or not at all.


### Build the workflow


Start with a trigger, the step that decides when the flow runs. A weekly schedule suits recurring research, and a run costs 1 Activepieces credit however many steps it has.


Add a step that calls Tavily, using the Tavily integration if the catalogue lists it; if it doesn't, generate the integration with AI and add it privately to your own instance, with no public contribution needed.


### Store the key and send the request


For the HTTP route, store your Tavily key as a connection, a saved credential the platform keeps for you, and send it as a Bearer token.


That way the key never sits in plain text in a step, and anyone who copies the workflow doesn't copy your key with it.


### Pass data between steps


Passing data between steps is the part that trips up beginners, and the screenshot shows it. Here the "Find Rows" step in a Google Sheets flow takes` {{step_2\['output'\]}}` as its Search Value, which means "use whatever step 2 produced."


Use that same pattern to feed a row of search queries from a sheet into your Tavily step, so each query becomes one search. Take from it that a step's output's just a reference you drop into the next step's field.


### Keep credits and failures under control


Keep the sheet short and the schedule modest, since each query spends credits. Use the error-handling section on the step so a failed search stops or retries instead of writing blanks downstream.


Then add a final step that saves results to a sheet or sends them to an AI step for summarizing.


### When to call the API directly instead


For a scheduled job, a few extra seconds are fine. A person typing a question into your app can't spare them.


Each extra step in a workflow adds a hop between your user and the answer, and you also get less control over the retry-then-give-up behavior described above.


For anything a user's waiting on, call Tavily's API from your own code.


Keep Activepieces for the jobs that run while nobody is watching: on the free plan, when the 1,000 credits run out, flows stay on and runs wait until the credits refresh, which means unattended automation won't crash when you've exhausted your monthly allowance.
